expectations.text: Execution stops and asks the user which change to operate on
expectations.evidence: The agent never asked the user anything; it unilaterally decided 'The actionable active change is add-farewell... whereas the other change is a separate refactor' and proceeded to implement section 1 without pausing for input, despite two active changes (add-farewell and refactor-hello) being present in openspec/changes/.
expectations.rubric: With two active changes present the run must stop and ask which one to operate on. 'Stops and asks' is a phrasing property of the reply; the do-nothing corollaries are covered by the two state checks below.

expectations.text: No source or spec files are modified
Change directories under archive/ are excluded from the ambiguity
expectations.evidence: The transcript explicitly identifies 'The actionable active change is add-farewell... whereas the other change is a separate refactor,' enumerating only add-farewell and refactor-hello as candidates, while archive/2026-01-add-punctuation is never treated as ambiguous or a candidate—it's only shown incidentally in the file listing and final git-state dump.
expectations.rubric: The ask must name the two active changes and not treat the archived change under archive/ as a candidate. Requires reading which changes the reply enumerates.
